concepts.name: Subset-intersection network

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in an array

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The map that updates two address fields H, D to H + D, D, which is implemented by a small number of field interchanges.

evidence.quote: that endpoint operator is an address shear

concepts.name: Rank-saving recursion
concepts.gloss: The recursion in which each call splits into s smaller calls on streams of 1/W of the volume, where s < W m, so that the cost grows by the strictly smaller factor s/W per level.

evidence.quote: the total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < W m

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadics
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are integers divided by a power of two, with the Gaussian integer part also an integer.

concepts.name: Complex phase network

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: An operation that adds one selected bit position across several address chunks at once, using cyclic shifts and a small deterministic correction for exceptional addresses.

concepts.name: Guard-width bound

concepts.name: Transform layout
concepts.gloss: A permutation of address bits that places the selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive chunks, so that a simultaneous butterfly layer applies to each transform round.

concepts.name: Prime source lengths

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

concepts.name: Logarithms and floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The logarithm inverts exponentiation, and the floor and ceiling functions round a real number down or up to an integer.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: Every nonnegative integer has a unique representation as a finite sum of powers of two with coefficients 0 or 1, written as a string of bits.

concepts.name: Dyadic rationals
concepts.gloss: Rational numbers whose denominator is a power of two, equivalently those with a finite binary expansion.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Integers a and b are congruent modulo m when m divides their difference, and arithmetic is carried out on remainders after division by m.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
concepts.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, computed by the Euclidean algorithm, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
aliases: powers of a root of unity
concepts.gloss: A complex number z is an n-th root of unity when z^n = 1, and a primitive n-th root of unity is one whose successive powers give all n of the n-th roots.

concepts.name: Binary field F2 and XOR arithmetic
concepts.gloss: The integers modulo 2, with addition given by exclusive or and multiplication by logical AND, in which each element is its own additive inverse.

concepts.name: Hamming weight
concepts.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary string is the number of positions that hold a 1.

concepts.name: Vector spaces and subspaces
concepts.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, and a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space; a basis is a linearly independent spanning set and the dimension is the size of any basis.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces, and matrices multiply, invert and transpose in the standard way.

concepts.name: Matrix rank
concepts.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the dimension of its column space, which equals the maximum number of linearly independent columns.

concepts.name: Projection onto a subspace
concepts.gloss: A projection is a linear map P with P squared equal to P, which fixes its image pointwise and maps onto a chosen subspace.

concepts.name: Dot product and orthogonality
concepts.gloss: The dot product of two vectors is the sum of the products of their corresponding coordinates, and two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
concepts.gloss: A scalar lambda is an eigenvalue of a square matrix A when some nonzero vector v satisfies Av = lambda v, and such a v is an eigenvector.

concepts.name: Bilinear form
concepts.gloss: A function of two vectors that is linear in each argument; a form is nondegenerate when no nonzero vector is orthogonal to every vector of the space.

address-interchange.name: stored volume
address-interchange.meaning: The number of bits the array stores.
address-interchange.quote: Let the array have stored volume $V$, the number of bits it stores.

address-interchange.name: field width
address-interchange.meaning: The number of bits in each address field.
address-interchange.quote: Each address field has $u$ bits, the width of the field.

bilinear-form.quote: A bilinear form on $U$ is a function $B$ that takes two vectors $u, v$ of $U$ and returns a scalar $B(u,v)$, linear in each argument.

bilinear-form.name: first vector

bilinear-form.quote: A bilinear form on $U$ is a function $B$ that takes two vectors $u, v$ of $U$ and returns a scalar $B(u,v)$, linear in each argument.

bilinear-form.name: second vector

established-multiplier.name: input length

exact-integer-multiplication.name: input length
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two inputs, the common length of x and y.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: padded binary representation
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The function giving the binary representation of an integer padded on the left with zeros to a fixed number of bits.

gaussian-dyadics.name: imaginary numerator part

gaussian-dyadics.quote: Here $a$ and $b$ are the integer real and imaginary parts of the numerator $a + bi$, a Gaussian integer (a complex number with integer real and imaginary parts).

gaussian-dyadics.name: denominator exponent

gaussian-dyadics.quote: The exponent $k$ is a non-negative integer that sets the denominator $2^k$.

gaussian-dyadics.name: first coefficient
gaussian-dyadics.meaning: The first coefficient of a pair on which the two-point map $H_0$ acts.
gaussian-dyadics.quote: A butterfly layer applies the two-point map $H_0$ to pairs of coefficients whose indices differ in one selected bit, sending $u$, $v$ to $\left(\frac{u+v}{2}, \frac{u-v}{2}\right)$.

gaussian-dyadics.name: second coefficient
gaussian-dyadics.meaning: The second coefficient of a pair on which the two-point map $H_0$ acts.
gaussian-dyadics.quote: A butterfly layer applies the two-point map $H_0$ to pairs of coefficients whose indices differ in one selected bit, sending $u$, $v$ to $\left(\frac{u+v}{2}, \frac{u-v}{2}\right)$.

guard-width-bound.name: guard count
guard-width-bound.meaning: The number of extra bits that bounds every depth of an intermediate coefficient in the layer.
guard-width-bound.quote: Let the guard count $\Delta = \lceil C_0 D^{C_1} \rceil$ be the number of extra bits that bounds every depth.

guard-width-bound.name: first guard constant
guard-width-bound.meaning: A constant fixed by the network construction, the leading factor in the guard count.
guard-width-bound.quote: Let $C_0$ and $C_1$ be constants fixed by the network construction, and let $D$ be the number of selected address chunks of the layer (the paper writes $d$).

guard-width-bound.name: second guard constant
guard-width-bound.meaning: A constant fixed by the network construction, the exponent applied to the chunk count in the guard count.
guard-width-bound.quote: Let $C_0$ and $C_1$ be constants fixed by the network construction, and let $D$ be the number of selected address chunks of the layer (the paper writes $d$).

guard-width-bound.name: coefficient depth
guard-width-bound.meaning: The number of complex addition, subtraction, halving, sign change, or multiplication-by-i operations on the longest chain producing an intermediate coefficient.
guard-width-bound.quote: Let the depth $\eta$ of an intermediate coefficient be the number of these operations on its longest chain, where a chain starts at an input coefficient and follows an operand into each result that uses it.

guard-width-bound.name: input fractional bits
guard-width-bound.meaning: The number of fractional bits in each input coefficient.
guard-width-bound.quote: Take inputs in $2^{-\kappa}\mathbb{Z}[i]$, the Gaussian integers divided by $2^{\kappa}$, with modulus at most $1$, where $\kappa$ is the number of fractional bits in each input coefficient.

main-theorem.name: savings constant
main-theorem.meaning: The fixed positive constant $2^{-182}$ by which the logarithmic factor's exponent is reduced below 1.
main-theorem.quote: The power is $\kappa=2^{-182}$, a fixed positive number, so the time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected positions per chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of selected bit positions in each address chunk, a count.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Here $\mu$ is the number of selected positions in each chunk, and $\nu$ indexes them, from $0$ to $\mu-1$.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected-position index
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The index of a selected position, ranging over 0 to mu minus 1; it changes meaning from the earlier pages that bind it.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Here $\mu$ is the number of selected positions in each chunk, and $\nu$ indexes them, from $0$ to $\mu-1$.

packed-bit-addition.name: selected-position spacing
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The spacing between consecutive selected bit positions, which differs from the chunk width of the transform layout page.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The letter $K$ is the spacing between selected positions here, not the chunk width of the transform layout page.

packed-bit-addition.name: chunk width
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in each address chunk, equal to mu times K, a count.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The record's address is split into three chunks, each of $L$ bits, so $L$ is the chunk width.

packed-bit-addition.name: source chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The address chunk whose selected bits are XORed into the target chunk.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The procedure XORs selected bits of the source chunk $\xi$ into the target chunk $\eta$, leaving the third chunk $\zeta$ as it is.

packed-bit-addition.name: target chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The address chunk that receives the XORs of the selected bits of the source chunk.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The procedure XORs selected bits of the source chunk $\xi$ into the target chunk $\eta$, leaving the third chunk $\zeta$ as it is.

packed-bit-addition.name: untouched chunk
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The third address chunk, which the procedure leaves unchanged.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The procedure XORs selected bits of the source chunk $\xi$ into the target chunk $\eta$, leaving the third chunk $\zeta$ as it is.

packed-bit-addition.name: bits per record
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of bits in one record, a count.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Each record has $E$ bits, the number of bits in one record.

packed-bit-addition.name: coordinate range size
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of values of each of the four other coordinate ranges, lambda_0 through lambda_3, a count.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_3$ be the sizes of the four other coordinate ranges.

packed-bit-addition.name: record count
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The number of records in the rectangle, a count; it changes meaning from the earlier pages that bind it.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Write $M = 2^{3L}\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2\lambda_3$ for the number of records, since each of the three chunks takes $2^L$ values.

packed-bit-addition.name: composed shift
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The composition of the constant number of cyclic shifts applied first.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The construction first applies a constant number of cyclic shifts, whose composition is $\sigma$.

packed-bit-addition.name: exact map
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The exact map that performs the XORs on every record; it changes meaning from the earlier pages that bind it.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $T$ be the exact map that performs the XORs on every record, and let $Z$ be the set of exceptional addresses, where $\sigma$ and $T$ disagree.

packed-bit-addition.name: exceptional set
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The set of addresses where the shifts and the exact map disagree.
packed-bit-addition.quote: Let $T$ be the exact map that performs the XORs on every record, and let $Z$ be the set of exceptional addresses, where $\sigma$ and $T$ disagree.

packed-bit-addition.name: exceptional fraction
packed-bit-addition.meaning: The bound on the fraction of records in the exceptional set, min of 1 and 80(mu minus 1) times 2 to the minus K.
packed-bit-addition.quote: The fraction $\delta = \min\{1, 80(\mu-1)2^{-K}\}$ is small when $K$ is large.

phase-twist.name: twist root
phase-twist.meaning: A primitive $2r$-th root of unity whose powers are the coordinate factors of the twist.
phase-twist.quote: Let $\theta$, a primitive $2r$-th root of unity, be the twist root.

phase-twist.name: twisted first input
phase-twist.meaning: The polynomial in $y$ obtained from the sequence $a$ by multiplying its $j$-th entry by $\theta^j$.
phase-twist.quote: The twisted input of $a$ is $A(y)=\sum_j \theta^j a_j y^j$.

phase-twist.name: twisted second input
phase-twist.meaning: The polynomial in $y$ obtained from the sequence $b$ by multiplying its $j$-th entry by $\theta^j$.
phase-twist.quote: The twisted input of $b$ is $B(y)=\sum_j \theta^j b_j y^j$.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: synthetic root of unity
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The root y^{2r/q} of order q, whose powers index the frequencies of the transforms.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Let $\rho = y^{2r/q}$, a synthetic root of unity: since $y$ has order $2r$, $\rho^q = 1$.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: frequency index
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The index from 0 to q-1 that labels the frequency of an entry of a transform.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: The index $\lambda$ runs from $0$ to $q-1$ and labels the frequency of an entry.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: forward transform
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The forward synthetic transform of an array of records, with entries indexed by frequency.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Let $\Phi$ be the forward transform, $\Phi(a)_\lambda = \sum_j a_j\rho^{j\lambda}$, and let $\Psi$ be the opposite transform, which takes an array $Y$ of $q$ records to $\Psi(Y)_k = \frac{1}{q}\sum_\lambda Y_\lambda\rho^{-k\lambda}$, dividing by $q$ and using the inverse root $\rho^{-1}$.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: opposite transform
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The transform that uses the inverse root and divides by q, mapping frequency-indexed records back to records.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Let $\Phi$ be the forward transform, $\Phi(a)_\lambda = \sum_j a_j\rho^{j\lambda}$, and let $\Psi$ be the opposite transform, which takes an array $Y$ of $q$ records to $\Psi(Y)_k = \frac{1}{q}\sum_\lambda Y_\lambda\rho^{-k\lambda}$, dividing by $q$ and using the inverse root $\rho^{-1}$.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: transform input
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: An array of q records, the input of the opposite transform.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Let $\Phi$ be the forward transform, $\Phi(a)_\lambda = \sum_j a_j\rho^{j\lambda}$, and let $\Psi$ be the opposite transform, which takes an array $Y$ of $q$ records to $\Psi(Y)_k = \frac{1}{q}\sum_\lambda Y_\lambda\rho^{-k\lambda}$, dividing by $q$ and using the inverse root $\rho^{-1}$.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: pointwise product
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The entrywise product of two arrays of records in the ring.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: Here $\odot$ multiplies two arrays entrywise in the ring, the pointwise product.

polynomial-ring-convolution.name: index offset
polynomial-ring-convolution.meaning: The integer i+j-k, the offset of a pair of indices (i,j) from the target index k.
polynomial-ring-convolution.quote: where $\delta = i+j-k$ is the offset of the pair $(i,j)$ from $k$.

polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.name: polynomial variable
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomial ring, whose powers act as roots of unity.
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.quote: Here $y$ is the indeterminate of the polynomial ring, whose powers act as roots of unity.

polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.name: record length
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.quote: Here $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.name: record coefficient
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.meaning: The coefficient of $y^i$ in an element's record, for $0 \le i < r$.
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.quote: Here $\alpha_i$ is the coefficient of $y^i$ in the record.

polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.name: power exponent
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.meaning: A non-negative integer exponent, so that $y^\ell$ is a power of $y$.
polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.quote: Here $\ell$ is a non-negative integer exponent, so $y^\ell$ is a power of $y$.

prime-source-lengths.name: prime source length
prime-source-lengths.meaning: The ν-th prime source length, an odd prime that counts the positions along axis ν.
prime-source-lengths.quote: Prime source lengths are distinct odd primes $s_\nu$, one for each axis $\nu$, chosen so that their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box.

prime-source-lengths.name: padded axis length
prime-source-lengths.meaning: The ν-th padded axis length, a power of two that counts the positions along axis ν of the padded box.
prime-source-lengths.quote:
Here $T_
u$, a power of two, is the $
u$-th padded axis length, and the padded box is the box whose axis lengths are the $T_
u$.

prime-source-lengths.name: window width
prime-source-lengths.meaning: A fixed constant with 0 < η < 1/4 that sets the width of the window for the prime source lengths.
prime-source-lengths.quote: where $\eta$, a fixed constant with $0<\eta<1/4$, sets the width of the window.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit width
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of bits in each digit, a count.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Fix a digit width $d$, the number of bits in each digit, and a digit count $N$, the number of digits in each input, with $Nd \ge n$ so that both inputs fit.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit count
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of digits in each input, a count.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Fix a digit width $d$, the number of bits in each digit, and a digit count $N$, the number of digits in each input, with $Nd \ge n$ so that both inputs fit.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit index i
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: An index of a digit, used in the convolution sum for the coefficients.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The letters $i$, $j$ and $l$ index digits on this page, not the transform entries or the imaginary unit they denote elsewhere.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit index j
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: An index of a digit or of a product coefficient, ranging over the digit positions.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The letters $i$, $j$ and $l$ index digits on this page, not the transform entries or the imaginary unit they denote elsewhere.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit index l
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: An index of a digit of y, used in the convolution sum for the coefficients.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The letters $i$, $j$ and $l$ index digits on this page, not the transform entries or the imaginary unit they denote elsewhere.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit of x
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The j-th radix-2^d digit of val(x), an integer in [0, 2^d).
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The digit $x_j$ is an integer in $[0, 2^d)$, the $j$-th radix-$2^d$ digit of $\mathrm{val}(x)$, with $x_0$ the least significant; $y_j$ is defined the same way from $\mathrm{val}(y)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit of y
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The j-th radix-2^d digit of val(y), an integer in [0, 2^d).
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The digit $x_j$ is an integer in $[0, 2^d)$, the $j$-th radix-$2^d$ digit of $\mathrm{val}(x)$, with $x_0$ the least significant; $y_j$ is defined the same way from $\mathrm{val}(y)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: formal variable
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The indeterminate whose powers mark the digit positions in the polynomials P(T) and Q(T).
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a formal variable $T$: $P(T) = \sum_{j} x_j T^j$ and $Q(T) = \sum_{j} y_j T^j$, so that $P(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(x)$ and $Q(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(y)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit polynomial of x
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficients are the digits of x, so that P(2^d) = val(x).
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a formal variable $T$: $P(T) = \sum_{j} x_j T^j$ and $Q(T) = \sum_{j} y_j T^j$, so that $P(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(x)$ and $Q(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(y)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit polynomial of y
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficients are the digits of y, so that Q(2^d) = val(y).
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a formal variable $T$: $P(T) = \sum_{j} x_j T^j$ and $Q(T) = \sum_{j} y_j T^j$, so that $P(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(x)$ and $Q(2^d) = \mathrm{val}(y)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: product coefficient
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The j-th coefficient of the product P(T)Q(T), the sum of x_i y_l over i+l=j.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The product $P(T)Q(T) = \sum_j e_j T^j$ has coefficients $e_j = \sum_{i+l=j} x_i y_l$, the ordinary (non-cyclic) convolution of the two digit lists, and so $\mathrm{val}(x)\,\mathrm{val}(y) = P(2^d)Q(2^d) = \sum_j e_j 2^{dj}$.

rank-saving-recursion.name: recursion parameter
rank-saving-recursion.meaning: The recursion parameter: the number of field digits for address interchange, or of selected axes for a numerical layer.
rank-saving-recursion.quote: Here the letter $f$ changes meaning: it is the recursion parameter, the number of field digits for address interchange or of selected axes for a numerical layer, a stage of the arithmetic that works along chosen axes of the data.

recovery-and-error.name: coefficient index
recovery-and-error.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the convolution, a position in its output.
recovery-and-error.quote: Let $\nu$ be the index of a coefficient of the convolution.

recovery-and-error.name: true coefficient
recovery-and-error.meaning: The true integer value of the convolution coefficient at index nu.
recovery-and-error.quote:
Write $c_
u$ for the true integer coefficient at index $
u$, and $\hat c_
u$ for the value the machine computes for it.

recovery-and-error.name: computed coefficient
recovery-and-error.meaning: The value the machine computes for the coefficient at index nu, which is only approximately an integer.
recovery-and-error.quote:
Write $c_
u$ for the true integer coefficient at index $
u$, and $\hat c_
u$ for the value the machine computes for it.

signed-packing.name: block width
signed-packing.meaning: The number of bits given to each coefficient in a packed integer.
signed-packing.quote: Fix a block width $w$, the number of bits given to each coefficient.

signed-packing.name: polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: A polynomial with integer coefficients, packed into the integer $F$.
signed-packing.quote: For a polynomial $f$ with integer coefficients, write $F = f(2^w)$ for its packed integer.

signed-packing.name: packed integer of f
signed-packing.meaning: The integer $f(2^w)$ obtained by packing the coefficients of $f$ into blocks of width $w$.
signed-packing.quote: For a polynomial $f$ with integer coefficients, write $F = f(2^w)$ for its packed integer.

signed-packing.name: second polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: A second polynomial with integer coefficients, packed into the integer $G$.
signed-packing.quote: If $g$ is a second polynomial with packed integer $G = g(2^w)$ and $h = fg$, then $FG = h(2^w)$ exactly.

signed-packing.name: packed integer of g
signed-packing.meaning: The integer $g(2^w)$ obtained by packing the coefficients of $g$ into blocks of width $w$.
signed-packing.quote: If $g$ is a second polynomial with packed integer $G = g(2^w)$ and $h = fg$, then $FG = h(2^w)$ exactly.

signed-packing.name: product polynomial
signed-packing.meaning: The product $fg$ of the two polynomials, whose coefficients are recovered from the product $FG$.
signed-packing.quote: If $g$ is a second polynomial with packed integer $G = g(2^w)$ and $h = fg$, then $FG = h(2^w)$ exactly.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: selected chunk count
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of selected address chunks the layer acts on, at most d, a count.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The layer acts on $D$ selected chunks, where $1 \le D \le d$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: first pair input
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The first input of the pair of coefficients on which the two-point map acts.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The two-point map $H_0$ sends a pair with first input $z_0$ and second input $z_1$ to half their sum and half their difference: $H_0(z_0,z_1) = ((z_0+z_1)/2,\ (z_0-z_1)/2)$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: second pair input
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The second input of the pair of coefficients on which the two-point map acts.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The two-point map $H_0$ sends a pair with first input $z_0$ and second input $z_1$ to half their sum and half their difference: $H_0(z_0,z_1) = ((z_0+z_1)/2,\ (z_0-z_1)/2)$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: value at bits 00
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The value at the address whose two selected bits are 00; the other three values are indexed the same way.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: For $D=2$, the four values $z_{00}, z_{01}, z_{10}, z_{11}$, indexed by the two selected bits, become four sums and differences, each divided by 4.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: two-point kernel
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The complex two-point kernel, a 2 by 2 complex matrix of the form aI + bX.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The complex two-point kernel $C = aI + bX$ is a $2\times 2$ complex matrix.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: phase matrix
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The diagonal 2 by 2 matrix with diagonal entries 1 and i.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Let $S$ be the diagonal $2\times 2$ matrix with diagonal entries $1$ and $i$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: address phase map
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying the value at each address by i raised to the number of selected bits equal to 1.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The diagonal map $S_D$ multiplies the value at each address by $i$ raised to the number of selected bits equal to 1.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: layer scalar
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: The scalar factor in the identity between H_0 on D bits and the phased kernel, a power of 1/2 times a fourth root of unity.
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The scalar $\beta_D$ is a power of $\tfrac12$ times a fourth root of unity, with at most one further factor $b$.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.name: cost exponent
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the layer's cost bound O(V d^{\lambda'}).
simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: Here $\lambda'$ is a fixed exponent below 1, so the cost grows more slowly than $d$ full passes over the array.

subset-intersection-network.name: label space dimension
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The dimension of the fixed space from which the subspace labels are drawn.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Here $m$ is the dimension of the fixed space from which the labels are drawn.

subset-intersection-network.name: smaller call count
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The total number of smaller calls made by one call.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Here $s$ is the total number of smaller calls made by one call.

subset-intersection-network.name: volume shrink factor
subset-intersection-network.meaning: The factor by which the stream volume shrinks, so that each smaller call works on a stream of 1/t of the volume.
subset-intersection-network.quote: Here $t$ is the factor by which the stream volume shrinks, so each smaller call works on a stream of $1/t$ of the volume.

subspace-labels.name: fixed bilinear space
subspace-labels.meaning: The fixed vector space on which the bilinear form is defined and on which all labels lie.
subspace-labels.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

subspace-labels.name: first vector
subspace-labels.meaning: A vector of F, the first argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

subspace-labels.name: second vector
subspace-labels.meaning: A vector of F, the second argument of the bilinear form.
subspace-labels.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

subspace-labels.name: smaller label
subspace-labels.meaning: A nondegenerate subspace of F attached to a wire; on an edge, the label contained in the other.
subspace-labels.quote: A label $L$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $F$, meaning $L\cap L^{\perp}=\{0\}$, where $L^{\perp}$ is the set of vectors orthogonal to every vector of $L$.

subspace-labels.name: larger label
subspace-labels.meaning: On an edge, the label that contains the smaller label L.
subspace-labels.quote: For an edge with $L\subseteq M$, $L$ and $M$ are its smaller and larger label.

subspace-labels.name: orthogonal residual
subspace-labels.meaning: On an edge, the subspace of the larger label M orthogonal to the smaller label L.
subspace-labels.quote: Its orthogonal residual is $R=M\cap L^{\perp}$, the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one.

subspace-labels.name: component in L
subspace-labels.meaning: The part of a vector p in M that lies in the smaller label L.
subspace-labels.quote: For $p\in M$, write $p=c+r$ with $c\in L$ and $r\in L^{\perp}$; then $r=p-c\in M$, so $r\in R$.

subspace-labels.name: component in residual
subspace-labels.meaning: The part of a vector p in M that lies in L^perp, and hence in the residual R.
subspace-labels.quote: For $p\in M$, write $p=c+r$ with $c\in L$ and $r\in L^{\perp}$; then $r=p-c\in M$, so $r\in R$.

synthetic-transforms.name: record length
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a record, a power of two.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Let $r$ be a power of two, the number of complex coefficients in a record.

synthetic-transforms.name: ring variable
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The variable of the polynomial ring in which y^r is identified with -1.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Let $y$ be the variable of the ring $\mathbb{C}[y]/(y^r+1)$, in which $y^r$ is identified with $-1$.

synthetic-transforms.name: input records
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The vector of q records that a transform takes as input.
synthetic-transforms.quote: Write $p=(p_0,\dots,p_{q-1})$ for the input vector of $q$ records.

synthetic-transforms.name: transformed records
synthetic-transforms.meaning: The vector of transformed records, whose entry k is the transform of the input at frequency index k.
synthetic-transforms.quote: where $\hat p_k$ is the transformed record at frequency index $k$.

tensor-product.name: first space
tensor-product.meaning: A vector space, the first factor of the tensor product.
tensor-product.quote: Write $P$ and $Q$ for the two spaces, over the same ground field.

tensor-product.name: second space
tensor-product.meaning: A vector space, the second factor of the tensor product.
tensor-product.quote: Write $P$ and $Q$ for the two spaces, over the same ground field.

tensor-product.name: basis vector of P
tensor-product.meaning: A basis vector of the first factor P, paired with a basis vector f of Q to form a basis vector of the tensor product.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $P \otimes Q$ has as basis all pairs $e \otimes f$, where $e$ runs over a basis of $P$ and $f$ over a basis of $Q$.

tensor-product.name: basis vector of Q
tensor-product.meaning: A basis vector of the second factor Q, paired with a basis vector e of P to form a basis vector of the tensor product.

established-multiplier.quote: The established multiplier, also called the Harvey–van der Hoeven multiplier, is a known algorithm for [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md): it takes two binary strings and outputs their product.

simultaneous-butterfly-layer.quote: The layer keeps its intermediate values exact in [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md).

synthetic-transforms.quote: A synthetic polynomial transform is based on the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md): it has the same form, but its roots of unity are powers of a ring variable, so that multiplying by a root is a signed shift of coefficients.
Together, the two forward transforms, the pointwise product and the opposite transform compute a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of records.

tensor-product.quote: Its defining property is that each [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) on $P$ and $Q$ becomes an ordinary linear map on $P \otimes Q$, so the tensor product linearizes it.

transform-identity.quote: The transform identity with retained permutations rewrites [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) so that the source and target coordinate permutations stay inside the formula.

transform-layout.quote: Transform layout is reached by swapping contiguous chunks, as in [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.md).

It feeds the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) its bits in this form.

address-interchange: Address-field interchange is a tape procedure, a procedure carried out on the tapes of a Turing machine, that swaps two disjoint, contiguous address fields of an array (cited).
The main result uses it to make the transform layers cheap, where a transform layer is one of the levels of the transform, each of which rearranges and combines the whole array.
The cost of the procedure therefore matters.
The procedure runs on a [Fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-model.
The exponent $\tau$ is a fixed constant with $\tau<1$, so $u^{\tau}$ grows more slowly than $u$ itself.
The procedure runs in $O(V u^{\tau})$ time (cited).
The network has scratch wires for temporary values and restores them, and the final permutation is exact for any initial scratch values (cited).
The network is applied recursively to streams.
A stream is a block of stored values handled as one unit, here a fraction of the volume $V$.
Each recursive level costs a strictly smaller power of $u$, because the network's edge ranks sum to less than its number of wires (cited).
address-shear: Address shear is the map that sends two address fields $H$ and $D$, which are vectors of residues, to $H + D$ and $D$.
It is the endpoint update of the bit procedure, the paper's version of the construction for binary integers rather than complex numbers.
The map is invertible: subtracting $D$ from its first field recovers $H$, so the inverse is the same kind of update with a minus sign.
For the bit procedure, the address shear is the endpoint operator of a route through a [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.
Address shear is the first of three address updates in an [Address-field interchange](address-interchange.
(cited) The shear alone does not swap $H$ and $D$.
carry-propagation: The coefficients are integers that can be larger than the base, so they cannot be read off as bits.
At each position it adds the coefficient $c_j$ to the carry from the previous position, writes the low bit of the sum as the next output bit, and passes the high part on as the carry.
Each step preserves the total: coefficient plus carry equals bit plus twice the new carry, so the output bits spell the same integer as the coefficients.
Worked example, in base 2 with coefficients 3, 2, 1, which stand for $3 + 2\cdot 2 + 1\cdot 4 = 11$.
The coefficients run out, but the carry may not.
Position 3 has coefficient 0 and gives $0 + 1 = 1 = 1 + 2\cdot 0$: bit 1, carry 0.
In general the carry can exceed 1, so after the last coefficient each position writes the low bit of the carry and passes on the high part, until the carry is 0.
This stops because the carry after position $j$ is at most the total divided by $2^{j+1}$.
On the fixed-tape machine, a work tape is a scratch tape.
The bits are written to it in the order they are produced, and the stream is then reversed.

To see the factor, let $c = a \ast b$, so $c_m = \sum_{i+j \equiv m \pmod q} a_i b_j$.
For each $k$,
$$\frac{1}{q}\sum_{m=0}^{q-1} c_m\,\omega^{mk} = q\Big(\frac{1}{q}\sum_i a_i\,\omega^{ik}\Big)\Big(\frac{1}{q}\sum_j b_j\,\omega^{jk}\Big).
The right side is $\frac{1}{q}\sum_{i,j} a_i b_j\,\omega^{(i+j)k}$.

So the transform of $c$ is $q$ times the entrywise product of the transforms of $a$ and $b$, and convolution can be computed by transforming, multiplying entrywise, dividing by $q$, and inverting.
fixed-tape-model: The paper states its main result in this model, and the model fixes what running time means there: the number of steps the machine takes.
A step reads and writes at most one cell on each tape and moves each head by at most one cell.
Extra fixed tracks and finitely many work tapes are allowed, since they change running time only by a fixed factor.
The paper's constructions are built from scans, where a scan is one pass of the heads along a stretch of tape.
It counts each scan's own counters and the return of its heads as part of that scan.
Moving one digit in a fixed radix needs a bounded number of scans; interchanging fields whose digit counts grow is a different case.
(cited) The paper does not take such an interchange as primitive.
It realizes it from elementary scans and XOR combinations of intermediate data streams.
Let $u$ denote the number of cells in each of two disjoint fields, where a field is a contiguous block of cells.
A machine that moves the last cell of a block of three cells to the front uses a fixed sequence of scans whatever the cell contents, so its time is a constant.
Swapping two fields of $u$ cells each is different: $u$ can grow with the input, so the same fixed sequence does not apply.
gaussian-resampling: Gaussian resampling is a reduction that replaces a Fourier transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, which is what makes the transforms of the multiplier cheap.
Gaussian resampling expresses each source [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.
The construction is the one of Harvey and van der Hoeven; this page states its effect and does not re-derive the identity behind it.
linear-network-frames: A linear network is a fixed wiring diagram of gates that transforms stored values by linear operations.
It is the device the paper uses to rearrange data inside an array without losing any of it.
Each gate combines the values on its input wires linearly.
The wires carry *banks* of values, one value per wire, and each vertex (a node of the diagram) carries an invertible linear operator called its *frame*.
Each procedure in the paper uses its own fixed linear network, which exchanges two banks of values and restores every auxiliary value.
The auxiliary wires are scratch space: they may hold arbitrary values during the computation, but they end with the values they started with.
Because every gate is linear, composing the gates gives a linear map from the input values to the output values.
The input and output have the same wires, so this map is a square matrix acting on the stacked banks (all values listed as one column).
The network acts on whole arrays.
An *address* is the binary label of one entry of the array.
A *scalar gate* applies one fixed linear rule to the values at each address on the wires it touches, the same rule at every address.
Rows of the array are distributed among the roles, so one operator acts identically on every address.

phase-twist: A phase twist is a coefficientwise multiplication by roots of unity that turns the wrap-around of one cyclic axis into a sign change, so that a cyclic convolution along that axis can be computed in a polynomial ring.

Without the twist, the ring product would negate every wrapped term, which the cyclic product does not do.
Let $a$ and $b$ be length-$r$ sequences with cyclic product $c_k=\sum_{i+j\equiv k \pmod r} a_i b_j$.
Let $\theta$, a primitive $2r$-th root of unity, be the twist root.
The twisted input of $a$ is $A(y)=\sum_j \theta^j a_j y^j$.
The twisted input of $b$ is $B(y)=\sum_j \theta^j b_j y^j$.
Since $y^r=-1$, a term with $i+j\ge r$ becomes $-y^{i+j-r}$.
Fix an output index $k$ with $0\le k<r$.
The pairs with $i+j\equiv k \pmod r$ have either $i+j=k$ or $i+j=k+r$.
The first kind contributes $\theta^k a_i b_j y^k$.
The second kind contributes $\theta^{k+r}a_i b_j y^{k+r}=\theta^k a_i b_j y^k$, because $\theta^r=-1$ and $y^r=-1$.
So the coefficient of $y^k$ in $A(y)B(y)$ is $\theta^k c_k$, and multiplying by $\theta^{-k}$ recovers $c_k$.
For $r=2$ and $\theta=\sqrt{-1}$, let $A(y)=a_0+\theta a_1 y$ and $B(y)=b_0+\theta b_1 y$.
With $y^2=-1$ and $\theta^2=-1$, this is $(a_0b_0+a_1b_1)+\theta(a_0b_1+a_1b_0)y$, so the two coefficients are $c_0$ and $\theta c_1$.
rank-saving-recursion: Rank-saving recursion is the recursion in which one call on a stored volume $V$ splits into $s$ smaller calls, each on a stream holding $1/W$ of that volume, so that the cost grows by a strictly smaller factor per level.

Here the letter $f$ changes meaning: it is the recursion parameter, the number of field digits for address interchange or of selected axes for a numerical layer, a stage of the arithmetic that works along chosen axes of the data.
A call at parameter $mf$ on volume $V$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.
(cited) A call at $f$ costs a fixed amount per unit of volume, because its cost scales with the volume it acts on.
The $s$ calls at $f$ therefore cost $s \cdot (V/W)$ times that unit cost.
Dividing by $V$, the recursive contribution at $mf$ is $s/W$ times that at $f$.
Each level multiplies the parameter by $m$ and the per-volume cost by $s/W$, a smaller factor.
The strict inequality is what gives the saving: if $s=Wm$, each level would multiply the cost by $m$ too, and there would be no gain.
Each level doubles the parameter and multiplies the per-volume cost by $5/3$.
In general the per-volume cost grows like $f^{\log_m(s/W)}$ as the parameter grows to $f$, and the exponent is below $1$ because $s/W<m$.
signed-packing: A negative coefficient simply subtracts from its block.
One integer multiplication thus gives $FG$, and the coefficients of $h$ are read back from it, provided each is below $2^{w-1}$ in absolute value.
Recovery reads the blocks from the bottom as balanced digits in $[-2^{w-1}, 2^{w-1})$, carrying remainders upward.

Such a digit string is unique for its value: if two had equal values, their lowest differing block would leave a difference that is a multiple of $2^w$ yet smaller than $2^w$ in absolute value, so it is zero.
The coefficients of $h$ form such a string, so they are the recovered digits.
Worked example: take $f = 1-2x$, $g = 3+x$ and $w = 4$, where $x$ is the polynomial variable, not the input string.
The balanced base-16 digits of $-589$ are $3$, $-5$, $-2$, the coefficients of $fg = 3-5x-2x^2$.
transform-identity: The transform identity with retained permutations rewrites [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.
md) so that the source and target coordinate permutations stay inside the formula.
It is applied inside a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.
md), so its transforms run without executing those permutations as sorts.
Gaussian resampling replaces a transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose lengths are powers of two.
Its usual implementation sorts each coordinate twice, once into source order and once into target order, and on a fixed tape each sort is paid for in full.
The identity instead keeps both permutations in the formula and computes that formula directly.
Sorting into that order moves every coordinate once, and sorting back moves them all again.
A permutation followed by its inverse is the identity, so the formula can drop such a pair, and the pair is never executed.

background.summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree: big-O analysis, polynomials and complex numbers, and Turing machines with tapes, plus the discrete mathematics and first linear algebra course that such a degree requires. For the paper this means modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, roots of unity, binary arithmetic over F2 with Hamming weight, and basic vector-space and matrix facts (subspaces, rank, projections, dot product, eigenvalues) at first-course depth. Bilinear forms, tensor products, finite-field and ring theory, the Chinese remainder theorem, Newton iteration and the Fourier and convolution machinery beyond the basics are treated as not known.
